name: Markel Group Inc.
moat_justification: Specialty-insurance-led conglomerate (a 'mini-Berkshire' structure) with disciplined niche underwriting, conservative reserving, permanent float that funds equities and Markel Ventures, and a decades-long compounding culture - one notch above the plain P&C peers scored 5 in this sweep because of that three-engine model. Capped at 6, not 7-8: the core product is re-shopped at renewal with no switching costs or network effect, pricing is cyclical, and earnings are driven by investment markets and reserve estimates that have produced recurring charges. A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.3%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low

The Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows in the same 10-K lists no share-based compensation addback line, and EDGAR companyfacts carries no ShareBasedCompensation / AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense fact for 2023-2025.); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
one_liner: High-quality specialty-insurance conglomerate, moat 6/10 - but sector-mismatched for an OE DCF and priced above value on current TTM cash flow: Tier C, weighted IRR 12.95%, weighted IV@15% $1,514.69 vs $1,825.00 price; it clears 15% only at or below $1,514.69.
moat_for: Specialty underwriting niche - hard-to-place risks (equine, museums, camps, specialty casualty) with less direct competition and a long disciplined record; Q2 2026 Markel Insurance combined ratio 93%
Permanent-capital three-engine model - insurance float funds a public equity portfolio and Markel Ventures' majority-owned businesses, diversifying cash flow beyond underwriting
Conservative reserving and low leverage culture - reserves set to be more likely redundant than deficient per the FY2025 10-K, net debt $339,106,000 in dcf_numbers.json
Buyback and capital discipline - share count shrinking 2.3%/yr in dcf_numbers.json, with repurchases funded from earnings
moat_against: Core insurance product has no switching costs or network effect - specialty cover is re-bid at renewal and pricing is cyclical across P&C

Earnings and OCF are hostage to investment markets and reserve estimates - net investment gains were $1,076,081,000 in FY2025 in the 10-K income statement, and H1 2026 carried a $205 million State National reserve charge
Reserve and legacy risk is recurring, not theoretical - CATCo run-off, State National collateral shortfall, social inflation in US casualty
Conglomerate complexity and key-person capital allocation - the Gayner investment edge and Ventures deal flow are people and reputation, not a structural barrier

overrides.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26), Consolidated Statements of Changes in Equity: 'Equity awards expensed' $54,982 thousand in 2025, $53,302 thousand in 2024 and $35,787 thousand in 2023 ($ in thousands in that statement). The Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows in the same 10-K lists no share-based compensation addback line, and EDGAR companyfacts carries no ShareBasedCompensation / AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense fact for 2023-2025.
